headline: Lamine Yamal honours childhood home with headband during World Cup semifinal
summary: The Spanish star's headband featured the postal code and name of Rocafonda, the Mataró neighbourhood where he grew up.
details: Spain and Barcelona youngster Lamine Yamal wore a headband with the inscriptions '08304' and 'Rocafonda' during Spain's 2-0 win over France in the 2026 FIFA World Cup semifinal in Dallas.

headline_marked: Tigers seek redemption: [[Bangladesh face Zimbabwe in first T20I]] in Bulawayo
headline: Tigers seek redemption: Bangladesh face Zimbabwe in first T20I in Bulawayo
summary: After losses in the Test and ODI series, stand-in skipper Tawhid Hridoy leads the squad as they look to turn the tide in the shortest format.
details: Bangladesh will take on hosts Zimbabwe in the first T20I in Bulawayo on Wednesday. The team hopes a change of venue from Harare to Bulawayo will bring a change in fortunes after defeats in the one-off Test and the subsequent ODI series.
Stand-in skipper Tawhid Hridoy emphasized that the Tigers must reduce mistakes to bounce back. He noted that the T20 format and the different venue conditions will provide a fresh start for the team.

The squad has seen several changes. Mosaddek Hossain has been drafted into the T20I side following strong performances in Australia ODIs, while Taskin Ahmed replaces Mustafizur Rahman, who is out with a hamstring injury.

Regular captain Litton Das remains unavailable, having been rested for the T20I series and ruled out of the ODIs due to a calf muscle strain. This absence has previously left the middle order lacking control and patience.

The series offers a chance for bowling all-rounders Mohammad Saifuddin and Abdul Gaffar Saqlain to secure regular spots. Yasir Ali also returns to the format after not featuring since the 2022 T20 World Cup.

Bangladesh will rely on a bowling attack featuring Nahid Rana, Shoriful Islam, and Taskin Ahmed. The team is drawing confidence from a seven-wicket victory in the final ODI and the form of Tanzid Hasan Tamim and Shoriful.
Zimbabwe, led by captain Sikandar Raza, will look to maintain their dominance. Their attack, led by Richard Ngarava and Blessing Muzarabani, aims to continue challenging the Tigers' batting line-up.
caption:
Can the Tigers turn the tide? After losing the Test and ODI series, Bangladesh starts their T20I campaign against Zimbabwe today.

Bangladesh will take on hosts Zimbabwe in the first T20I in Bulawayo on Wednesday. The team hopes a change of venue from Harare to Bulawayo will bring a change in fortunes after defeats in the one-off Test and the subsequent ODI series.

Stand-in skipper Tawhid Hridoy emphasized that the Tigers must reduce mistakes to bounce back. He noted that the T20 format and the different venue conditions will provide a fresh start for the team.

The squad has seen several changes. Mosaddek Hossain has been drafted into the T20I side following strong performances in Australia ODIs, while Taskin Ahmed replaces Mustafizur Rahman, who is out with a hamstring injury.

Regular captain Litton Das remains unavailable, having been rested for the T20I series and ruled out of the ODIs due to a calf muscle strain. This absence has previously left the middle order lacking control and patience.

The series offers a chance for bowling all-rounders Mohammad Saifuddin and Abdul Gaffar Saqlain to secure regular spots. Yasir Ali also returns to the format after not featuring since the 2022 T20 World Cup.

Bangladesh will rely on a bowling attack featuring Nahid Rana, Shoriful Islam, and Taskin Ahmed. The team is drawing confidence from a seven-wicket victory in the final ODI and the form of Tanzid Hasan Tamim and Shoriful.

Zimbabwe, led by captain Sikandar Raza, will look to maintain their dominance. Their attack, led by Richard Ngarava and Blessing Muzarabani, aims to continue challenging the Tigers' batting line-up.
